newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees sustained farm sector growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees sustained farm sector growth in 1997.

text.p: The Philippine farm sector is expected to keep growing this year after expanding 3.9 percent in value in 1996, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said on Wednesday.
"We hope to grow not lower than 3.9 percent this year with recovery prospects in the coconut and the fisheries subsectors and better crop harvests," Escudero told a news conference.
The sector grew by a modest 1.7 percent in 1995.
"The growth last year was within the three to five percent target we have set at the start of the year," Escudero said.

The production value in the sector, which includes crops, fisheries, poultry and livestock, grew to 230.479 billion pesos in 1996 from 221.819 billion pesos the previous year, the Agriculture Department said.
Escudero said better rice, corn and sugarcane harvests and improved performances of the hog and poultry subsectors in 1996 offset losses in the fisheries industry, which has been hurt by overfishing.

For 1997, Philippine unmilled rice output is expected to reach 12 million tonnes under the government's rice productivity programme. The 1996 output was 11.283 million tonnes, below the government's estimate of 11.5 million but higher than 1995's 10.54 million tonnes.
Corn harvests were expected to increase to 5.2 million tonnes this year, up from 4.15 million tonnes in 1996 and 4.128 million tonnes in 1995.
The government will extend funding credit for fertilisers and better seeds again this year to improve rice and corn yields, Agriculture Department officials said.

Agriculture Undersecretary Domingo Panganiban said the government hopes to increase the average unmilled rice yield per hectare this year to between four and five tonnes, up from three tonnes in 1996.
Escudero said in a previous interview he expected the Philippines to import between 300,000 and 500,000 tonnes of rice this year and up to 500,000 tonnes of corn.
"The rice importation is for buffer purposes during the lean months of July to September," he said.

Escudero said he had asked livestock and poultry farmers to import the corn they need instead of asking the National Food Authority (NFA) to import for them. Farmers usually ask the NFA to import corn because the state agency can do this duty free.
The NFA said rice imports reached 890,000 tonnes in 1996 and corn imports 500,000 tonnes.
The gross value of the crops subsector jumped by 15.92 percent to 271.8 billion pesos at current prices against the previous 234.493 billion pesos.

The gross value of the livestock subsector grew by 15.59 percent to 77.666 billion pesos from 1995's 67.193 billion, while the poultry subsector was up 11.21 percent to 53.672 billion pesos from the year-ago 48.263 billion.
